result: acted: THE "BROKEN MAC" WAS A NODE VERSION, AND I HAD IT WRONG FOR DAYS. .github/workflows/mac-runner-auto.yml has no actions/setup-node step — the only lane running on ambient node, at 24.18.0, while review-hub-ci.yml pins 22 at three jobs. The Mac's own preflight.log shows 209 gates green then gate 214 dying on `Error: setTypeOfService EINVAL` thrown from `writeH1` inside node's OWN bundled undici on v24.18.0, before the load driver sees a response; the load test reaches port 5321 through global fetch, which is undici. That also explains the earlier ECONNRESET to ::1:5321 — reset was the symptom, the throw is the cause. Fix open as #789 (preflight PASSED 320 gates with /v1 under concurrency GREEN on node 22, breadth 56, both parity gates green). ITS OWN MAC JOB IS THE EXPERIMENT and was still in_progress at this reading, so nothing is claimed about the Mac going green — a linux box cannot produce a macOS result. THE CORRECTION I OWE: I escalated this to the owner as a PHYSICAL LOOK at that machine on a firewall hypothesis. I labelled it a hypothesis and escalated on it anyway, sending a person at hardware while the answer sat in an artifact I could have downloaded at any point. Withdrawn, on the PR and in a send op to the mac lane this cycle. The Mac broke no written rule either — engines.node is ">=22", which 24 satisfies — so no gate could have caught it, and the reason it went unseen is that mac-runner-harness.yml PRINTS `node -v` and nothing compares it.
